idea-plugin.name: CodeCall Map
idea-plugin.description:
CodeCall Map

An open-source call-chain recorder for Java, built to answer one question: where does my program actually spend its time?

  • Dedicated Run/Debug mode — pick CodeCallMap in the Run configuration dropdown and the javaagent is injected automatically. Debug mode works the same way, so you can still set breakpoints on the slow method itself.
  • Automatic package detection — no manual setup. The plugin derives the packages to monitor from the package of your main class and the module source roots (similar in spirit to Spring's {@code @ComponentScan}). You can also specify packages by hand, or combine both.
  • Automatic instrumentation — method-level bytecode instrumentation via ASM. No manual tracing code, no recompilation of your business classes. The call tree and per-method timing are recorded for you.
  • Hot-spot analysis — ranked by self time = total time − child call time, so the methods that are slow themselves surface first. Results can be aggregated per class.
  • Waterfall and sequence diagrams — visualize call relationships against the timeline, with exceptions and slow calls highlighted.
  • Jump to source — click any span to open the exact method it came from.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 or later (Ultimate).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.2.63：Complete sequence diagram, faster tab switching, tidier editor hints.
    · Sequence diagram now shows the whole round trip — besides the solid call arrow it draws the dashed return arrow, plus an activation bar that spans from a call to its return, and lifelines stay pinned while you scroll.
    · Tab switching no longer stalls. Canvas panels used to allocate a canvas as tall as the entire call list and repaint all of it on every switch. They now draw only the visible viewport, so switching between tabs is instant and each panel keeps its scroll position.
    · Editor hints no longer cover your code. Parameter values move out of the code line into a single end-of-line summary (▶ 12ms · 3 params · has return · 1/3). Click the summary or the gutter icon to open a read-only dialog with the full arguments, return value and exception; when a method ran several times, step through the recordings with Previous / Next.
  • 1.0.1.60：Localized description, version separation for 2025.2 / 2025.3.
    · Plugin description and change notes are now available in Chinese and English; the IDE picks the matching one from your UI language.
    · The 2025.2 build is published as 1.0.1.60-legacy so it can coexist with the 2025.3 build under one plugin ID.
    · Fixed packageRelease picking up a stale artifact from the previous branch build, which could put the wrong plugin inside a zip.
  • 1.0.0.60：First open-source release. Everything below was built during internal iteration (0.x) and ships together in this release.
    · Inline recorded data in the editor — click an arrow in the sequence diagram to open the method and see the recorded call laid onto the source: parameter hints after each argument, a gutter summary line (▶ 12ms · 3 params · has return · 1/3), and a gutter icon for the full arguments, return value and exception. When a method was called several times, click the 1/N counter to cycle through the recordings.
    · Return values — the exit probe branches by return type (throwing / void / value). Values live in separate files under ret/<spanId>.json instead of being inlined into the JSONL, which would otherwise inflate single lines to megabytes.
    · Standard UML sequence diagram — rewritten from a Gantt-style bar chart. Participants are numbered in call order with the entry point on the left. Messages follow pre-order traversal of the call tree, because timestamps only have millisecond precision and start-time ordering would put child calls before their parents.
    · Argument trimming — collections, maps and arrays stop at 200 elements and report how many were omitted; the total payload is capped at 256 KB with 4096 characters per string. Previously only an 8 MB circuit breaker existed, so a list of tens of thousands of rows could stall the main thread and then be discarded as one useless _overflow marker.
    · Hang fixes — argument serialization no longer recurses through diamond references (an object graph where several fields point at the same object used to expand exponentially; a single object is now visited once and repeats are written as <duplicate>). Regex patterns are compiled once instead of per filter check.
    · Self-diagnostics — instrumentation timing statistics, slow-call stack dumps, a watchdog that dumps all thread stacks when collection stalls, and an instrument-report.txt listing every instrumented class and method.
    · Spring Boot port number — read from SpringApplicationAdminMXBean. Builds on 2025.2 additionally need the Spring Boot plugin declared as an optional dependency, because plugin class loaders are isolated by default.
